content.text: {"title":"The Museum of Small Things","premise":"In a sunny shed behind the library, Ada and Ben open a museum for overlooked treasures with Pip the magpie. Ada wants a grand opening, Ben wants every borrowed thing returned proudly, and Pip wants the ridiculous prize: the shiniest button in the whole collection. Their choices decide whether the museum becomes a respectful exhibit, a surprising trade, or a performance for one very particular visitor.","cast_and_props":"Characters: Ada (wants a dazzling opening; curiosity 2), Ben (wants borrowed treasures respected; kindness 2), Pip the magpie (wants the Shiniest Button; mischief 2). Props: museum.box (owner Ada, open/closed), red.marble (owner Ben, borrowed from his baby sister), brass.key (owner Ada, found in a coat pocket), blue.button (owner Pip, his prize), visitor.card (invitation for the library keeper), display (empty/ordinary/sparkling), museum.owner (Ada/Ben/Pip), exhibit.mode (quiet/tour/performance), visitor.mood (unknown/delighted/puzzled). Keep all state keys prefixed by an existing entity ID.","kernels_and_interactions":"Use 4 families: discovery/knowledge (observe and tell about box contents and ownership); possession (transfer props only from current owners); curation (choose display and exhibit mode); social performance (invite the keeper, perform a guided sound-and-story tour, record the keeper's response). Ada's observation of the box must enable her to choose what to display. Ben's knowledge that the marble is borrowed must enable a return-or-ask action. Pip's knowledge of the button's owner must enable a trade or a comic refusal. Reuse opening the museum, telling a fact, arranging the display, and greeting the visitor across paths. A pivotal turn should change Pip's desire from 'keep' to 'share' or Ben's agreement from 'return' to 'lend.'","seed_parameters":"Use random.Random(seed) to select initial conditions from three meaningful seed branches, without exposing a branch number: (A) the box contains the red marble and the invitation is already written; (B) Pip has secretly placed the blue button in the box and Ada believes the box holds only dull objects; (C) the library keeper arrives early, believing the museum is a quiet collection rather than a noisy tour. Seed also varies whether Ben initially trusts Pip with the display. Encode chosen conditions as actual initial scalar properties named in premise_keys: box contents, invitation status, visitor expectation, and Pip/Ben agreement.","candidate_scenes":"Aim for 16 candidates and 5–9 selected events. Shared: open_box (Ada opens box after observing it), inspect_contents (Ada observes box.contents), tell_contents (Ada tells Ben), invite_keeper (Ada transfers visitor.card to Ben or sets invitation delivered), arrange_display (Ada sets display), greet_visitor (Ben greets keeper), tour_display (Ada performs quiet tour). Problem 1, mistaken belief: discover the blue button is Pip's and Ada's planned 'dull things' display becomes sparkling; Pip may trade it for the brass key. Problem 2, conflicting ownership: Ben finds the red marble in the box, asks to borrow it properly, or returns it to his sister before opening; the final exhibit is smaller but trusted. Problem 3, expectation mismatch: the keeper arrives expecting silence; Ada chooses a whisper-tour, while Pip chooses a noisy button concert if agreement fails. Include tell_keeper_expectation, request_lend_marble, return_marble, trade_button_for_key, perform_whisper_tour, perform_button_concert, and visitor_response. Mark only the Pip-sharing turn and Ben's lend/return decision pivotal.","constraints":"Declare every slot before use; 12–22 candidates, scalar values only, no counters. Use observe, tell, and transfer meaningfully. Every action needs guarded access, ownership, knowledge, or motive conditions. The inciting action is Ada's invitation/opening promise, establishing the actual problem before responses. Goals should accept distinct concrete outcomes: display.status in {trusted, dazzling, surprising} and visitor.mood in {delighted, puzzled}; outcome_keys should include display.status, exhibit.mode, and visitor.mood. Do not make all preparation pivotal. Catalog every candidate scene, including preview paths. Use conditional prose for contents, ownership, expectation, and results; never imply an unseen discovery or an unused prop.","different_endings":"Trusted opening: the red marble rests beside a note from its owner, and the keeper smiles at the tiny empty space it left behind. Dazzling opening: Pip's blue button catches the sun while the brass key hangs beside it, and Pip bows to his own glittering reflection. Whisper-tour opening: Ada leads the keeper through a hush of small wonders, while Pip's feathers tremble with unplayed music. Puzzled-concert ending: Pip taps the button, key, and box in a ridiculous rhythm; the keeper blinks, then places one tiny bell beside the display. Sharing ending: Pip gives up the button temporarily for the tour, and the museum's brightest thing is the place where it will return."}
